observationsNotFindings: The one thing I pressed hardest on was whether naming v6 as predecessor while calling the file v8 skips a version. It does not, and the structure is better than the sibling pattern: v6 is the last RECORDED predecessor under D-145 and is pinned as predecessor; v7 is the immediate but REJECTED draft and is pinned separately at predecessorV7 with its digest and the digest of the verdict that rejected it. Every other repair-successor I reviewed this session collapsed those two roles into one field because their rejected predecessor was also their recorded one. Here they differ, and the file says so.

The gates array is byte-identical between v7 and v8, so the substantive naming work - thirty correct artifactExists claims, the eight added G23 through G30 entries, the G03 parent-v4 occupancy path - is unchanged. I re-audited it independently against the filesystem rather than carrying my v7 result forward, and it holds at thirty of thirty.

Eleven occurrences of the superseded 18/16/19 figures survive in v8. I classified each rather than sweeping on the count: two are declared DATED-D086-ERA under inheritedRecitals.fields, one is a historical record of a v2-era codex finding's repair, two are true prohibitions against presenting 16 as the denominator, and four are the statements that the arithmetic is retired. None asserts a superseded figure as current, and total rows=22 is gone entirely.
